titulo_es: Undefined: ogni, qualche, alcuni, nessuno, tutto

qualche.consejo: Undefined invariable followed by singular name.

texto: **Ogni** (each) and **qualche** (some / some) are necessarily combined with **singular** nouns: **ogni giorno** (each day), **qualche volta** (sometimes / sometimes).
On the other hand, **alcuni / alcune** (some) always goes with nouns in **plural**: **alcuni turisti**, **alcune amiche**.
**Niente** (nothing) and **nessuno** (no one / none) demand double denial when they go after the verb: **Non c'è niente** (there is nothing); **Non vedo nessuno** (I see no one).
**Tutto/a/i/e** is in line with the name and usually carries article before specific nouns: **tutti i giorni** (every day), **tutta la città** (the whole city).

frases.it: Ci sono tanti turisti in centro questo fine settimana?
frases.es: ¿Hay muchos turistas en el centro este fin de semana?
frases.en: Are there many tourists in the center this weekend?

frases.it: Sì, ci sono visitatori tutti i giorni, dal mattino alla sera.
frases.es: Sí, hay visitantes todos los días, desde la mañana a la noche.
frases.en: Yes, there are visitors every day, from morning to night.

frases.it: E nei musei c'è qualcosa di interessante da vedere?
frases.es: ¿Y en los museos hay algo interesante que ver?
frases.en: And is there something interesting to see in museums?

frases.it: Certo, ma oggi non c'è nessuna fretta: visitiamo con calma.
frases.es: Claro, pero hoy no hay ninguna prisa: visitemos con calma.
frases.en: Of course, but today there's no rush: let's visit calmly.

bloques.pregunta: How is «each day» translated into Italian in a correct way?

opciones.explicacion: «Ogni» is invariable and must accompany singular nouns.
«Qualche» can only be accompanied by names in singular.

bloques.pregunta: What is the right way to say «There's no one in the office.»?

opciones.explicacion: The negative construction requires «non» before the verb and «nessuno» as indefinite.
The order of denial in Italian requires that «non» be placed in front of the verb.

bloques.frase: Ci sono ___ persone in piazza stamattina.

opciones.explicacion: «Persone» is plural feminine substantive, so it matches «tante».

bloques.frase: Alcuni turisti hanno visitato il centro storico con la guida.

opciones.texto: An undetermined group of tourists visited the old town with a guide.
opciones.explicacion: «Alcuni turisti» indicates a partial and plural number of people.

opciones.texto: All the tourists preferred to stay at the hotel.
opciones.explicacion: That would be expressed with «tutti i turisti».

opciones.texto: No tourist hired a guided tour in the center.

bloques.pregunta: How often do you make the trip?
bloques.frase: Qualche volta prendo il treno per andare a Milano.

opciones.texto: Every now and then or sometimes.
opciones.explicacion: «Qualche volta» is equivalent to sometimes or occasionally.
That would be expressed with «ogni giorno» or «tutti i giorni».

opciones.texto: He's never used that train in life.
opciones.explicacion: That would be said with the «non … mai» warning.

bloques.frase: Lavoro tutti i giorni con impegno
bloques.traduccion: I work every day with dedication
bloques.explicacion: Temporary whole structure with «tutti i» in plural.

bloques.pregunta: What noun adequately completes the «qualche ___» expression?

opciones.explicacion: «Qualche» must be named in singular («qualche libro»).
Even if it makes plural sense, formal agreement requires singular.
It does not support intermediate partitive prepositions.

intro: Learn to quantify people and things without using exact numbers by the Italian indefinite.
